questions.question: At the beginning of therapy with Mark M., you discussed the possible duration of treatment and estimated that therapy would not extend beyond his insurance coverage of your fee. You also informed Mark that you would be unable to reduce your fee when his therapy was no longer covered by insurance. Unfortunately, that time has arrived as Mark's insurance will cover only the next three sessions, many of Mark's problems are still unresolved, and he cannot afford your full fee. In terms of ethical responsibilities, you are ____________________.

options.A: required to see Mark at a reduced or deferred fee until his problems are adequately resolved
options.B: required to see Mark at a reduced or deferred fee until he feels ready to terminate treatment
options.C: required to discuss the matter with Mark and make a referral at the end of the three sessions if necessary
options.D: not required to continue seeing Mark since you discussed this matter at the beginning of therapy

questions.explanation:
You are not required to continue seeing a client if the client cannot pay your fee. However, to avoid abandoning the client when insurance
coverage has ended, you should either offer services at a reduced or deferred fee or, if that is not feasible, make appropriate referrals. Standard
6.04 of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle II.32 of the Canadian Code of Ethics apply to this situation.
Answer A: This is incorrect as ethical guidelines do not require you to see a patient at a reduced or deferred rate.
Answer B: This is incorrect as psychologists are not required to provide services at reduced or deferred rates.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect because even though discussion of this issue at the beginning of therapy is a good practice, it does not
eliminate your responsibility to the client when his insurance ends.

questions.question: After a year in private practice, you hire a newly-licensed psychologist whom you will provide with an o�ce and secretarial services. You will also refer clients to the psychologist and pay him 50% of the fees he collects from those clients. This arrangement is ________________.

options.A: unethical because it involves barter
options.B: unethical because it involves being paid for client referrals
options.C: ethical as long as the psychologist is being compensated in an equitable way
options.D: ethical because, as an employer, you can determine the conditions of employment

questions.explanation:
Of the responses given, this one is the best. The arrangement described in this question seems somewhat dubious in terms of acceptability,
but the facts presented do not clearly indicate an ethical violation. One can quickly misread this question and think that the fee split is
based on the referral (which would be problematic between colleagues). But for two reasons, this scenario is actually ethical. 1) the
fee split is not between colleagues; it is between an employee and an employer and 2) the fee split is based on services rendered not
the referral. The employed psychologist is receiving 50% of the fee for providing therapy services and the employer psychologist is
receiving 50% of the fee for providing rent, o�ce supplies, scheduling, marketing, and clientele. This issue is addressed in Standard 6.07
of the Ethics Code and is discussed in the Ethics Manual of the written study materials.
Answer A: This is incorrect as ethical guidelines only address barter with clients, and barter is acceptable under some circumstances.
Answer B: This is incorrect as referral fees are not entirely prohibited by ethical guidelines.
Answer D: This is incorrect because it is not an accurate description of an employer's ethical responsibilities.

questions.question: Informed consent from a client _____________________________.

options.A: must always be in writing
options.B: must always be in writing and in the client's native language
options.C: may be either verbal or in writing
options.D: may be either verbal or in writing but must be documented

questions.explanation:
Standard 3.10 of the APA's Ethics Code states that consent must be "appropriately documented," and Principle I.22 of the Canadian Code of
Ethics states that it is permissible to "accept and document oral consents" when there is a good reason not to obtain signed written consent.
Answer A: This is incorrect, as informed consent must be documented, but ethical guidelines do not require consent to be written.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect because clinicians are responsible for documenting consent, but it may be verbal if documented.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect because it is a less complete answer than Answer D, which speci�es consent must be documented.

questions.question: Dr. Oliver Olivetti has been seeing a client for several months who recently changed jobs. The client learns her new insurance plan does not begin covering pre-existing conditions for 12 months. The client asks Dr. Olivetti to produce invoices so that it appears she has just started therapy. If Dr. Olivetti complies with the client's request, he is acting _____________________.

options.A: ethically since he is taking the client's welfare into consideration
options.B: ethically only if not to do so would require the client to quit therapy
options.C: ethically only if the insurance forms do not require him to sign a statement saying that treatment began after the effective date of the insurance
options.D: unethically

questions.explanation:
The client in this situation is asking Dr. Olivetti to commit insurance fraud and, if Dr. Olivetti does so, he will be acting both unethically and
illegally. Standard 6.04 of the APA's Ethics Code addresses this matter.
Answer A: This is incorrect because although Dr. Olivetti should consider his client's welfare, he would be acting unethically and illegally if he
agrees to the arrangement requested by the client.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect, as this arrangement would be illegal and unethical regardless of the rami�cations for the client.
Answer C: This is incorrect because this would still represent insurance fraud since the client and therapist are well aware of the insurance
provisions.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the status of professional (therapy) records?

options.A: The physical record belongs to the client.
options.B: The physical record belongs to the therapist.
options.C: The physical record belongs to the therapist, but the information contained therein belongs to the client.
options.D: The physical record and the information contained therein belong jointly to the therapist and the client.

questions.explanation:
While the actual physical record is the property of the therapist, laws require therapists to make the information contained in records available
to the client in most situations. This does not mean that a therapist must release the physical record to a client but, instead, that the therapist
may be required to show the client the record or provide the client with a summary or copy of it. The laws regarding professional records are
complex and vary somewhat from jurisdiction to jurisdiction. When answering questions like this one, you'll want to pick a general answer that
is likely to apply to most jurisdictions.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect as the client does not own the physical record.
Answer B: This is incorrect because it is a less complete answer than C. While the physical record does belong to the therapist, this answer
fails to address the complexity of the question, which is that the client has access to the contents of the therapy notes.
Answer D: This is incorrect because while the client has a right to the contents of the therapy records, the record itself belongs to the therapist.

questions.question: Dr. Bettina Browne, a licensed psychologist, undertakes a child custody evaluation at the request of the child's mother. The father agrees to be evaluated also, and Dr. Browne obtains signed informed consent from both parents before beginning her assessment. Dr. Browne administers the MMPI and Rorschach tests to both parents. The mother obtains signi�cantly elevated scores on the MMPI's K and L scales, suggesting that she tends to lie and to be excessively defensive, and these tendencies are con�rmed by her Rorschach responses. No signi�cant abnormality is suggested by the father's MMPI and Rorschach results. Based on the test results, Dr. Browne recommends that the mother not be awarded custody of the child. Dr. Browne ______________________.

options.A: has acted ethically because her evaluation included both parents
options.B: has acted ethically because the parents signed informed consents before the evaluation
options.C: has acted unethically because of her use of the MMPI and Rorschach tests as methods of evaluating the mothers parental suitability
options.D: has acted unethically because she made speci�c recommendations regarding custody rather than simply reporting the results of the evaluation

questions.explanation:
A psychologist is ethically required to use tests only for purposes for which they have been validated according to Standard 9.02 of the APA's
Ethics Code. Based on the information given, it appears that Dr. Browne has acted unethically by basing her custody recommendation on MMPI
and Rorschach test results since these tests have not been validated for this purpose. Even if the tests had been validated for this purpose, Dr.
Browne's recommendation should have been based on more than the results of only two tests.
Answer A: This is incorrect because even though the psychologist acted appropriately by evaluating both parents prior to making a
recommendation, response C. is a better answer.
Answer B: This is incorrect because obtaining signed informed consent does not overcome the problem of using the MMPI and Rorschach as
predictors of parental functioning, a purpose for which they have not been validated.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect because recommendations are acceptable as long as they are based on a thorough evaluation of all parties.

questions.question: Miranda M., age 32, makes an appointment with you at the recommendation of her physician who has diagnosed her with recurrent headaches due to stress. The woman tells you that a friend of hers was trained in self-hypnosis for tension headaches and says that she also would like to learn self-hypnosis. You took a weekend workshop on hypnosis in graduate school but have not used it in your clinical practice. As an ethical psychologist, you should _______________________.

options.A: admit your lack of expertise in the use of self-hypnosis and refer the woman to another therapist
options.B: advise the woman that the underlying cause of her headaches would probably not be dealt with by self-hypnosis and suggest that she begin individual psychotherapy
options.C: accept the woman for treatment and begin training her in self-hypnosis after reviewing your workshop notes
options.D: accept the woman for treatment and begin training her in self-hypnosis but obtain consultation if you encounter any problems during the course of treatment

questions.explanation:
Of the responses given, this one is most consistent with the requirement to provide services that are within the boundaries of your professional
competence. Note that, while it is up to you to determine your competence with regard to a particular service or technique, a weekend
workshop in self-hypnosis is clearly inadequate. Providing services within the boundaries of one's competence is addressed by Standard 2.01
of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle II.6 of the Canadian Code of Ethics.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect, as It would be unethical to try to convince the client to choose another course of treatment simply because
you are not trained in the treatment she desires.
Answer C: This is incorrect because reviewing your workshop notes would not be adequate training.
Answer D: This is incorrect because although this response comes closer to ful�lling the requirements of the ethical guidelines than do
responses B. and C., it falls short of those requirements because it implies that consultation would not be sought unless you believe that you
are having problems during the course of treatment.

questions.question: You have been hired to assist with a research project on process variables in group psychotherapy. The psychologist who is the principal investigator tells you to discourage participants from leaving the group prior to the end of the study because, if too many participants drop out, the study's potential usefulness will be seriously compromised. As an ethical psychologist, you should ____________________________________.

options.A: refuse to assist with the research project
options.B: immediately �le a complaint against the psychologist with the psychology licensing board or ethics committee
options.C: write a letter to the psychologist, indicating the relevant ethical standards and offering to discuss the matter with him
options.D: follow the psychologist's instructions since, by "discouraging" participants from leaving the group, you are not actually coercing them to participate

questions.explanation:
By offering to discuss the matter with the psychologist, you are attempting to resolve the matter informally, which is consistent with the
requirements of the ethical guidelines. Standard 8.02 of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle I.30 of the Canadian Code of Ethics both require
psychologists to allow participants to withdraw from a research study at any time.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect because resigning from the project would not correct the ethical violation.
Answer B: This is incorrect because although a report may eventually be necessary, it is not the best �rst step since this matter may be
amenable to an informal resolution.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect because this would be unethical, and you would be violating the provisions of Standards 1.04 and 1.05 of
the Ethics Code and Principles II.40 and II.41 of the Canadian Code of Ethics, which require psychologists to take action when a colleague acts
in an unethical way.

questions.question: A psychologist supervisor of several interns at a community hospital in a small town notices that one of the interns seems unenthusiastic and depressed. When he talks to her, she tells him that she's been very unhappy lately and feels she has no one to turn to. The intern asks the psychologist to see her in therapy, and he agrees to do so. The psychologist has acted ___________________________.

options.A: unethically by agreeing to get involved in a dual relationship
options.B: unethically by violating the intern's right to privacy
options.C: ethically because they are working in a community hospital in a small town
options.D: ethically because the intern is in desperate need of help

questions.explanation:
In most situations, psychologists should avoid multiple (dual) relationships. Standard 3.05(a) of the APA Ethics Code states that "a
psychologist refrains from entering into multiple relationships if the multiple relationships could reasonably be expected to impair the
psychologist's objectivity, competence, or effectiveness in performing his or her functions as a psychologist, or otherwise risks exploitation or
harm to the person with whom the professional relationship exists." The psychologist in the situation described is entering into multiple
relationships that may threaten his objectivity and effectiveness as a supervisor and therapist.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect as there is no indication that privacy is an issue in this situation.
Answer C: This is incorrect, because, in some circumstances, multiple relationships may be unavoidable. However, the fact that the intern and
psychologist work in a community hospital in a small town does not necessarily mean that no other options are available.
Answer D: This is incorrect, as there is no indication that the intern is in such "desperate need of help" that she cannot wait to see another
professional.

questions.question: A psychologist decides to use a computerized test service to facilitate scoring and interpretation of the MMPI-2, which he frequently administers to his clients. The psychologist should be aware that ____________________.

options.A: the use of computerized interpretations is prohibited by ethical guidelines
options.B: computerized scoring and interpretation services are notoriously unreliable
options.C: computerized interpretations should always be supplemented with other information obtained by the psychologist
options.D: because of their objectivity, computerized interpretations are preferable to subjective interpretations

questions.explanation:
Automated scoring and interpretation services are available for a number of psychological tests including the MMPI-2. The information in a
computerized interpretation is limited and, therefore, the best policy is to always supplement computerized interpretations with information
from other tests, interviews, and observations, according to Standards 9.02 and 9.09 of the APA's Ethics Code.
Answer A: This is incorrect because the use of automated interpretation services is not prohibited by ethical guidelines as long as certain
standards are met by both the service and the users of the service.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect, because the quality of computer interpretations varies from service to service, and it cannot be concluded
that all computerized interpretations are "notoriously unreliable."
Answer D: This is incorrect, as the information provided by computerized interpretations is limited, and the accuracy of the interpretation
depends on the quality of the service. Therefore, it cannot be concluded that computerized interpretations are necessarily the preferred method
of score interpretation.

questions.question: The term "insanity" is a ______________________.

options.A: popular term for a mental disorder
options.B: legal, nonpsychiatric term for certain types of mental disorders
options.C: psychiatric term that refers to a psychotic disorder with an unknown etiology
options.D: psychiatric term that refers to an organic mental disorder

questions.explanation:
The term "insanity" is used in the legal arena and is not a psychiatric term. Defendants who plead not guilty by reason of insanity are
contending that a mental disease or defect precluded them from understanding the difference between right and wrong. Insanity is a legal term
that varies in terms of its de�nition from jurisdiction to jurisdiction.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect, as "insanity" has a distinct legal meaning.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect, as the term "insanity" has a legal, not psychiatric, meaning.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect, because "insanity" is not a term used to describe a mental disorder.

questions.question: Alice A. has a master's degree in clinical psychology but is not licensed. She is hired by a community mental health clinic to administer several standard psychological tests to adults. According to ethical guidelines, this is ___________________.

options.A: acceptable as long as a professional clinical psychologist co-signs Alice's evaluations
options.B: acceptable as long as a professional clinical psychologist supervises Alice's activities
options.C: unacceptable since Alice is not a licensed psychologist
options.D: unacceptable since Alice does not have a doctoral degree

questions.explanation:
Ethical (and legal) guidelines do not prohibit the provision of all psychological services by individuals who are not licensed, clinical
psychologists. However, they do require that such persons be supervised by a licensed psychologist.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. Simply co-signing reports would not be considered adequate supervision.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect, because Alice may administer some psychological tests as long as she has been adequately trained and is
supervised by a licensed psychologist according to Standard 9.07 of the APA's Ethics Code.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect because having a doctoral degree is not required for the provision of psychological services, but supervision
by a licensed psychologist is required in this case.

questions.question: Following the retirement of his business partner, Dr. Sheldon Smith is the only psychologist in a small town with the closest mental health professional over 100 miles away. Several of Dr. Smith's new clients have problems for which he has limited training and experience. Dr. Smith should ____________________.

options.A: refuse to see the clients
options.B: see these clients but use only interventions that he has experience using
options.C: see the clients and obtain supervision or consultation by telephone
options.D: agree to see these clients only if they are in crisis

questions.explanation:
Rather than turning patients away, Dr. Smith should seek supervision to meet his clients' needs. Standard 2.01 of the APA Ethics Code states
that "When psychologists are asked to provide services to individuals for whom appropriate mental health services are not available and for
which psychologists have not obtained the competence necessary, psychologists ... may provide such services in order to ensure that services
are not denied if they make a reasonable effort to obtain the competence required by using relevant research, training, consultation, or study."
Answer A: This answer is incorrect, given the ethics code encourages psychologists to seek the training and supervision needed to meet
clients' needs when there are limited referral options available.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect, given the clients' needs, including the client's diagnosis and cultural background should determine the
mode of treatment delivered.
Answer D is incorrect. While delivering treatment in an emergency may be appropriate, this answer is less complete than Answer C.

questions.question: A 24-year-old woman calls Dr. Sylvia Silby for an appointment but refuses to discuss her problem on the phone. During the initial therapy session, the young woman discusses her di�culties in a vague, guarded manner, indicating that, for the past few months, she has had increasing di�culty sleeping and has felt anxious and irritable. Ten minutes before the end of the session, the young woman tells Dr. Silby that she has been seeing another therapist for six months and that four weeks ago they began having a sexual relationship. As an ethical psychologist, Dr. Silby should _______________________.

options.A: advise the woman to terminate treatment with the other psychologist and begin therapy with her
options.B: advise her of her rights and alternative courses of action
options.C: contact the other therapist to discuss the matter with them
options.D: �le a complaint against the other therapist with the ethics committee and recommend to the woman that she immediately terminate treatment with the other therapist

questions.explanation:
Of the actions listed in the answers, the best one is to discuss the matter with the client and advise her of her options. Ethical violations by
colleagues are covered in Standards 1.04 and 1.05 of the APA's Ethics Code and are discussed in the Ethics Manual of the written study
materials. Clearly, the original therapist has violated ethical guidelines and may have violated the law.
Answer A: In order to respect the client's autonomy, Dr. Silby should discuss with the client her options so the client can determine the next
steps.
Answer C: Dr. Silby cannot contact the therapist without the client's consent, since to do so would represent a breach of con�dentiality.
Answer D: Dr. Silby cannot make a report herself without the client's consent, as again, this action would be a breach of con�dentiality.

questions.question: Farris F. terminated therapy with Dr. Pamela Prince several months ago but calls to request an appointment due to feeling lonely and depressed. Farris also feels "like he wants to die." In the past two months, Dr. Prince has been reducing her caseload due to retirement. The best course of action in this situation is for Dr. Prince to ______________________________.

options.A: explain to Farris that she is reducing her caseload but that she is willing to counsel him by phone in case of an emergency
options.B: see Farris in therapy until the crisis has passed and then provide him with appropriate referrals
options.C: explain to Farris that she is no longer accepting clients and refer him to a colleague
options.D: provide Farris with several referrals and ask him to call her if none of those turn out to be satisfactory

questions.explanation:
Because the client states he "feels like he wants to die," the best course of action is to see the client in therapy until the crisis has passed, and
then provide him with appropriate referrals. This answer is most consistent with the "spirit" of the ethical guidelines. See, for example,
Standards 3.04 and 10.09 of the APA's Ethics Code and Principles II.2 and II.34 of the Canadian Code of Ethics.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. This response fails to prioritize the client's welfare in accordance with ethical mandates.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect as, again, it does not respond to the fact the client is experiencing a crisis.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. It, too, fails to account for the serious nature of the client's concerns.

questions.question: Dr. Wanda Weim, a licensed psychologist, receives a request to testify in a custody proceeding on behalf of a male client that was receiving conjoint marital therapy six months prior. He requests Dr. Weim to provide the court with information about his parenting skills and relationship with his spouse and children. Dr. Weim contacts the man's wife, who refuses to give the psychologist permission to testify. Dr. Weim should do which of the following?

options.A: testify as requested by the husband
options.B: testify only about matters pertaining to the husband
options.C: testify only about matters for which she is quali�ed to make a judgment
options.D: refuse to testify

questions.explanation:
Multi-client situations create special considerations and concerns about con�dentiality since it is not often possible to release information
about one client without also revealing con�dential information about another client. In this situation, both clients (the husband and wife) must
give their permission before Dr. Weim can release con�dential information. Therefore, she should refuse to testify, unless she is ordered to do
so by the court.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. Dr. Weim does not have permission to release information from one of the clients.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. Because therapy was conjoint, Dr. Weim will be unable to release information pertaining to one client
without releasing information about the other client.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. In this case, the primary concern is whether both clients grant permission for Dr. Weim to testify.

questions.question: You have started seeing a client who is from a different cultural background than you. She is having di�culty coping with the recent death of her mother. You have frequently worked with clients who are coping with loss, but you have never worked with a client from this background. You'd like to continue seeing this client in therapy to broaden your experience with culturally diverse populations. Your best course of action would be to ____________________________.

options.A: continue working with the client but proceed with caution
options.B: seek supervision or consultation and continue to work with the client
options.C: refer the client to another therapist who has experience working with clients from this background
options.D: explain the situation to the client and terminate therapy

questions.explanation:
This is addressed by Standard 2.01(b) of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle II.8 of the Canadian Code of Ethics. Standard 2.01(b) states
"where scienti�c or professional knowledge in the discipline of psychology establishes that an understanding of factors associated with age,
gender, gender identity, race, ethnicity, culture, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, disability, language or socioeconomic status is
essential for effective implementation of their services or research, psychologists have or obtain the training, experience, consultation, or
supervision necessary to ensure the competence of their services, or they make appropriate referrals."
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. To proceed with caution is insu�ciently vague, but seeking consultation or supervision is consistent with
the ethical guidelines.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. Given the therapist has previously worked with clients who have experienced loss, there is no indication
that a referral is necessary, particularly when the therapist can obtain consultation or supervision.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. It is both acceptable and desirable for psychologists to acquire new skills and to treat new problems,
provided they obtain appropriate supervision or consultation.

questions.question: After three sessions with a therapy client, Dr. Leonard Lykowski realizes that he's feeling somewhat hostile toward the client, because she reminds him of his wife whom he's currently divorcing. Dr. Lykowski's best course of action would be to _______________________________.

options.A: refer the client to another therapist without telling the client the reason for the referral
options.B: refer the client to another therapist after discussing the reason with her
options.C: recognize that his feelings are the result of countertransference and continue to work with the client
options.D: consult with another psychologist to determine whether or not to continue seeing the client in therapy

questions.explanation:
This issue is addressed in Standard 2.06 of the APA's Ethics Code and is discussed in the Ethics Manual of the written study materials. In this
situation, Dr. Lykowski's personal problems may be affecting his objectivity. Consultation with another professional is ordinarily the best course
of action whenever a therapist is concerned that a personal problem might interfere with one's ability to provide adequate therapy. While you
wouldn't simply terminate treatment due to countertransference, if you are unable to work through it and provide objective treatment,
termination may be applicable.
Answer A: Referring the client without an explanation is generally not consistent with sound practice and concern for the client's welfare.
Answer B: While Dr. Lykowski may decide to take this route as a last resort, he would serve the client better by consulting with another
professional to attempt to resolve the con�ict.
Answer C: Dr. Lykowski's feelings likely do, in fact, represent countertransference, but he would want to seek consultation to determine if those
feelings are negatively impacting his ability to provide the client with appropriate services.

questions.question: Dr. Jacob Mans�eld receives a subpoena requiring him to testify about a current therapy client. Dr. Mans�eld contacts the client who states that she does not want him to release any con�dential information to the court. Dr. Mans�eld should _____________________.

options.A: notify the attorney who issued the subpoena that the client has asserted the privilege and request that he be released from subpoena
options.B: do nothing further until he receives an order from the court to appear at the trial
options.C: notify the court that he will not be appearing at the trial because the client does not want him to do so
options.D: advise the attorney who issued the subpoena that he cannot appear as requested because the client has not given him permission to do so

questions.explanation:
A subpoena is a legal document that requires a psychologist to appear at a designated time in a legal proceeding. If the client invokes the
privilege by saying she does not want the therapist to release con�dential information to the court, the subpoena is still valid, and the
psychologist must appear unless he/she has been released from it. When the client invokes the privilege in this type of situation, the
psychologist should contact the client's attorney or his/her own attorney to discuss the matter. The psychologist can also contact the attorney
who issued the subpoena to request to be released from it.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. Psychologists should not ignore subpoenas. Unless the psychologist receives a written release, he/she
must appear as requested but would not reveal con�dential (privileged) information without the client's consent or without an order from the
court to do so.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. The psychologist should work through an attorney to obtain a release from the subpoena.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. Without a release from the subpoena, the psychologist must appear in court.

questions.question: You receive an email from Dr. Brenda Browne, a licensed psychologist, who is currently seeing one of your former clients for a substance use disorder. Dr. Browne asks you to forward the client's record to her and states that the client has signed a release authorizing you to do so. You should:

options.A: wait until you receive a request from the client before taking any action
options.B: contact the client to discuss the release of information
options.C: forward a photocopy of the �le to the psychologist as requested
options.D: forward a summary of the �le to the psychologist that includes only information related to the client's current condition

questions.explanation:
Even though the person requesting the client's record is a licensed psychologist, you would not want to breach con�dentiality by providing
con�dential client information to her without knowing speci�cally to what the client has consented to.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. It is unlikely the client would contact the psychologist directly to ask that records be forwarded.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. You would want to verify that the client has, in fact, signed a release and discuss the release and its
potential consequences with the client before providing the psychologist with the requested information.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. The primary concern, in this case, is to con�rm the client understands the consequences of releasing
information. Further, it may be di�cult to separate out which information is speci�c to the client's current presenting concerns.

questions.question: The term privilege refers to _____________________________.

options.A: an ethical requirement designed to protect client information from being disclosed except when the client has signed a release
options.B: a legal requirement designed to protect con�dential information from being disclosed to anyone not directly involved in a client's case
options.C: an ethical requirement that applies to the con�dentiality of therapist-client communications in both legal and nonlegal situations
options.D: a legal requirement designed to protect con�dential information from being disclosed in a legal proceeding

questions.explanation:
Privilege is a legal term and refers to "privileged communications" that arise in legally designated relationships (e.g., the therapist-client
relationship).
Answer A: This answer is incorrect, as it does not address the legal context of the term.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect, as to whether one is involved in a client's case is largely irrelevant in a legal setting.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect because privilege applies to a legal obligation. Privilege is discussed in the Ethics Manual of the written
study materials.

questions.question: A woman comes to family therapy with her three daughters, ages 10, 13, and 19, all of whom live at home with the woman and their father. During the third therapy session, the 19-year-old tells you that her father began sexually molesting her when she was 13 years old. When you ask the younger girls if their father has ever abused them, they are reluctant to say anything about their father, and the mother adamantly denies any knowledge of abuse. In this situation, you should _____________________________________.

options.A: advise the mother to contact the appropriate authorities
options.B: �le a report with the appropriate authorities yourself
options.C: meet with the father to determine if he is abusing the younger daughters
options.D: maintain con�dentiality since the known victim of abuse is over 18 years old

questions.explanation:
Whenever you acquire a reasonable suspicion in your professional capacity that a minor is being abused, you have a legal obligation to report
the abuse. Therefore, you would be legally required to �le a report with the appropriate authorities.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. As a professional psychologist, you are required to report suspected abuse, and would not rely exclusively
on a client who stated she �led a report.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. Your responsibility lies in reporting the abuse, but not in investigating it. Addressing it with the father may
interfere with the ability of proper authorities to investigate the concern.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. Although psychologists are not usually required to make a report when the individual is over the age of 18,
in the situation described in the question, you would have reasonable suspicion that the younger sisters are also victims of abuse. Additional
information about reporting child abuse is provided in the Ethics Manual of the written study materials.

questions.question: You receive a letter from Mrs. Bisque's attorney asking you to testify on behalf of Mrs. Bisque in a divorce settlement regarding the custody of her children. You are aware that Mrs. Bisque's husband was recently admitted to a psychiatric hospital in another city. You should _____________________________________.

options.A: make a recommendation based on your knowledge that Mr. Bisque is obviously unable to have custody of the children
options.B: make a recommendation based on an interview with Mrs. Bisque and her children
options.C: refuse to make a recommendation since psychologists are not supposed to make speci�c custody recommendations
options.D: refuse to make a speci�c recommendation about custody unless you can evaluate the entire family

questions.explanation:
Although it is not unethical to provide information (e.g., test results) about a single party in a custody dispute, it would be unethical to make a
recommendation about custody based on incomplete information. An accepted standard of practice in custody situations is that a
psychologist should not make a recommendation for custody unless the psychologist has evaluated all parties. This is consistent with the
requirements of Standard 9.01 of APA's Ethics Code and Principle II.13 of the Canadian Code of Ethics and with the provisions of the APA's
Guidelines for Child Custody Evaluations in Divorce Proceedings.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. The question does not indicate you have any knowledge of Mr. Bisque as a parent, given it does not state
you conducted an evaluation of the family.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. An interview with one parent is an insu�cient basis on which to make a custody recommendation.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. Psychologists may make recommendations regarding child custody provided they follow the ethical and
practice guidelines cited above.

questions.question: You receive a request from a psychologist working at a mental health crisis unit for information about a former client of yours who left three months ago with an outstanding balance of $500. Due to an emergency situation, the client has been admitted as an inpatient and has signed a release. You tell the psychologist that you will provide her with the information she has requested only after the client has made arrangements for paying his bill. You have ___________________________________.

options.A: acted ethically as long as you had informed the client of your policy regarding unpaid fees
options.B: acted ethically since the client has violated your implicit contract with him to pay the fee for the services you provided to him
options.C: acted ethically since this action is not covered by the ethical guidelines
options.D: acted unethically

questions.explanation:
In this situation, the former client's records are needed for an emergency situation as the client has been admitted as an inpatient to a mental
health crisis unit.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. The ethical guidelines prohibit "holding a client's records hostage" because the client has not paid his or her
bill when these records are requested and needed for emergency treatment.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. Again, withholding the client's records because of an outstanding bill would be unethical.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. See Standard 6.03 of the APA's Ethics Code which explicitly prohibits this practice and Principles II.1 and 2
of the Canadian Code of Ethics which require psychologists to promote the welfare of clients and to avoid harming them.

questions.question: Kameko K., a psychology intern, administers psychological tests for a community mental health clinic, but her supervisor always scores the tests and interprets the results. When preparing the psychological report for these clients, the supervisor does not indicate that the intern administered the tests. This is _________________________.

options.A: ethical because the supervisor scored and interpreted the tests
options.B: ethical because the supervisor is responsible for the accuracy of the psychological report
options.C: unethical because an intern should not be administering psychological tests
options.D: unethical because the intern should be listed as the examiner in the report

questions.explanation:
This issue is not directly addressed by ethical guidelines, so the best approach when choosing the answer would be to identify the one that is
most consistent with the "spirit" of the guidelines. In this case, Standard 5.01(b) of the APA's Ethics Code prohibits psychologists from making
misleading statements, and Standard 6.06 requires psychologists to provide accurate information to payors and funding sources. It is also
consistent with Principles III.1 and 5 of the Canadian Code of Ethics.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. In the interest of reporting accurate information, the psychologist should list the clinician who administered
the tests.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. Administering, scoring, and interpreting test results are critical components of a psychological evaluation.
To withhold the contributions of a clinician would not be in keeping with ethical requirements.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. Provided interns are trained in test administration, it is ethical for them to administer psychological tests
under supervision.

questions.question: A client of Dr. William Wong who has been in therapy for six months is currently the defendant in a court case. The client's attorney contacts Dr. Wong, requesting that he provide her with information regarding diagnosis and treatment progress. Dr. Wong should _______________________________.

options.A: release the information as requested since privilege is waived in this situation
options.B: release only the information he believes is relevant to the client's case
options.C: release the information since the request came from the client's attorney
options.D: discuss the release with the client before taking any additional action

questions.explanation:
The release of con�dential client information ordinarily requires a waiver of con�dentiality from the client. Privilege may or may not be waived
in this situation. Dr. Wong should discuss the release of con�dential information and obtain a waiver from the client before sharing information
with the attorney.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect because it fails to prioritize con�dentiality as the primary concern.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. Again, Dr. Wong needs to con�rm the client intends to release information to the attorney.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. Even though the client's attorney has contacted Dr. Wong, a release is still required. Dr. Wong cannot
determine whether the client intends to release information without consulting with her.

questions.question: During a discussion with a 4th-grade teacher, the teacher tells a school psychologist that one of her students is constantly disrupting the class. After evaluating the child and obtaining more information about the situation, the school psychologist concludes that the teacher's approach with the child is part of the problem. Consequently, the school psychologist should __________________________________.

options.A: make an appointment with the principal to discuss the teacher's approach
options.B: explain to the teacher how her approach may be exacerbating the problem
options.C: recommend that he (the therapist) start counseling the child on a regular basis
options.D: recommend that the child be transferred to another classroom

questions.explanation:
Although this situation is not explicitly addressed by ethical guidelines, the APA's Ethics Code and the Canadian Code of Ethics require
psychologists to cooperate with other professionals. School psychologists must often act as a coordinator to bring together a variety of people
and resources to resolve problems. Of the answers given, this one is most in line with the child's best interests and the school psychologist's
responsibility to work with all people involved in the case.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. General Principle B of the APA's Ethics Code states that "psychologists consult with, refer to, or cooperate
with other professionals and institutions to the extent needed to serve the best interests of those with whom they work." The child's teacher is
the most directly involved professional, and given that she asked for help, it makes sense to start with her.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. The question indicates the teacher's behavior is contributing to the problem. Depending on the child's
situation, individual therapy may be appropriate at some point, but this is not the best answer.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. Because the teacher asked for assistance, it makes sense, to begin with advising her what she can do
differently. Moving the child to a different classroom could be more disruptive for the child. This is not a reasonable choice.

questions.question: To serve as an expert witness in a court case, a psychologist must ______________________________________.

options.A: be board certi�ed as an expert witness
options.B: be quali�ed by the court to offer opinions and conclusions about the case
options.C: have been hired by the person he/she will be testifying about
options.D: testify only about what he/she personally observed or obtained

questions.explanation:
An expert witness is a person who, because of his/her special training, knowledge, or experience, is quali�ed to offer an opinion as testimony in
a court proceeding.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. Board certi�cation is not required to serve as an expert witness.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. Whether the psychologist is hired by the subject of his or her testimony is irrelevant.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. A lay witness or eyewitness testi�es regarding what he or she personally observed.

questions.question: Sally, age 14, tells her therapist that she wants to die and that she has access to her mother's sleeping medication. The therapist believes that Sally's threat is serious and tells Sally that he'll have to contact her parents. Sally states their agreement when beginning therapy was that all information provided would be con�dential. If the therapist contacts Sally's parents, he has acted ____________________.

options.A: unethically if Sally was, in fact, told that con�dentiality would be maintained
options.B: unethically if he contacts Sally's parents without �rst obtaining Sally's consent to do so
options.C: ethically as long as the limits of con�dentiality were discussed with Sally at the outset of therapy
options.D: ethically since a breach of con�dentiality is justi�ed when a client is threatening suicide

questions.explanation:
Psychologists are legally and ethically obligated to breach con�dentiality whenever a client is believed to be a danger to themselves. With
respect to choosing to tell her parents, the therapist acted ethically regardless of whether or not they clearly explained the limits of
con�dentiality at the start of therapy.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. Psychologists must take appropriate action whenever a client is suicidal.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. Because Sally is a minor, contacting her parents would be an appropriate action.
Answer C: While psychologists should discuss the limits of con�dentiality, whether or not this discussion took place, the psychologist should
still contact the parents to protect Sally.

questions.question: You receive a call from Mrs. Wang who is very upset because her 14-year-old daughter witnessed an assault of her best friend three days ago and is distraught. Her daughter has not slept, declines to eat, and is consistently tearful. You have limited experience working with adolescents and in providing crisis intervention. However, you are the most experienced psychologist in the community. As an ethical psychologist, you will _____________________.

options.A: agree to see Mrs. Wang's daughter in therapy since you've had some experience providing crisis intervention experiences
options.B: inform Mrs. Wang about your lack of experience and let her decide if she wants you to provide therapy to her daughter
options.C: inform Mrs. Wang that you cannot see her daughter because of your lack of experience
options.D: see Mrs. Wang's daughter in therapy only until the crisis has ended or until you locate alternative services

questions.explanation:
This answer is most consistent with ethical requirements. 2.02 of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle II.8 of the Canadian Code of Ethics apply
to this situation. 2.02 of the Ethics Code, for example, states that "in emergencies, when psychologists provide services to individuals for whom
other mental health services are not available and for which psychologists have not obtained the necessary training, psychologists may provide
such services in order to ensure that services are not denied. The services are discontinued as soon as the emergency has ended or
appropriate services are available."
Answer A: This answer is incorrect because it does not take into account the limited services that would be provided to address an emergency
situation.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. The psychologist needs to determine the degree to which she or he can address the client's needs given the
crisis.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. The ethical guidelines allow for �exibility in the case of a psychologist responding to an emergency
situation on a short-term basis.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the use of deception in research studies that may cause participants pain?

options.A: Deception is acceptable in studies that may cause pain only when the use of pain is justi�ed by the study's potential value.
options.B: Deception is acceptable in studies that may cause pain only when there are no alternative methods for conducting a study.
options.C: Deception is prohibited when the pain is physical but not when it is psychological in nature.
options.D: Deception is prohibited whether the pain is physical or psychological in nature.

questions.explanation:
This answer is most consistent with Standard 8.07(b) of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle III.24 of the Canadian Code of Ethics. Standard
8.07(b), for example, states that "psychologists do not deceive prospective participants about research that is reasonably expected to cause
physical pain or severe emotional distress." Pain in research is acceptable only when certain conditions are met.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. When pain is expected, the ethical guidelines do not weigh the potential contributions of the study.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. It does not align with ethical mandates.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. The ethical standards prohibiting deception apply to both physical and emotional pain.

questions.question: Dr. Calvin Claymore, a licensed psychologist, regularly waives the co-payment for low-income clients whose therapy fees are covered by insurance. This practice is:

options.A: ethical only if the insurance company has agreed to this arrangement
options.B: ethical since it is in the best interests of low-income clients
options.C: ethical as long as Dr. Claymore does not bill the insurance company for an increased hourly fee in order to collect her full fee
options.D: ethical as long as the insurance company does not explicitly prohibit this arrangement

questions.explanation:
The practice described in this question represents insurance fraud, which is both unethical and illegal. Most insurance companies agree to pay
a speci�c percentage of a psychologist's fee but, when the co-payment is waived, this means the insurance company is paying the entire fee.
Consequently, regularly waiving the co-payment without the permission of the insurance company represents insurance fraud.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. A psychologist who waives the co-payment when the insurance company has not agreed to the
arrangement is engaging in insurance fraud.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. Insurance companies that require patients to submit a co-payment mandate psychologists bill the patient
for his or her share.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. Psychologists who waive the co-pay because an insurance company has not explicitly prohibited it, risk
insurance fraud, which has serious legal and �nancial penalties.

questions.question: A psychologist receives a phone call from a person with whom the psychologist had an intimate relationship for a short period of time over two years ago. The relationship ended amicably, and this person wants to start therapy with the psychologist. With regard to ethical requirements, which of the following is true about this situation?

options.A: It would be ethical to begin therapy with this person as long as the psychologist does not revive their previous personal relationship.
options.B: It would be ethical to begin therapy with this person since two years have passed since the end of the relationship.
options.C: It would be ethical to begin therapy with this person as long as the psychologist discusses the potential con�icts of interest during the informed consent process.
options.D: It would be unethical to begin therapy with this person.

questions.explanation:
This answer is most consistent with Standard 10.07, which explicitly prohibits psychologists from accepting former sexual partners as therapy
clients, and Principle III.33 which prohibits multiple relationships that might impair a psychologist's objectivity.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. The APA ethical guidelines are clear that psychologists do not accept clients who are former sexual
partners.
Answer B. This answer is incorrect. There is no two-year timeframe for beginning therapy with former romantic partners, as ethical mandates
forbid such arrangements.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. Again, the ethical guidelines clearly prohibit therapeutic relationships with former sexual partners.

questions.question: When conducting research with human participants, a psychologist should be aware that ___________________________.

options.A: participants must be debriefed as soon as possible after their participation in the study, especially when the study has involved deception
options.B: participants must be debriefed after their participation in the study only if the psychologist believes that not doing so will result in harm to them
options.C: participants may be debriefed after their participation when deception occurs
options.D: participants must be debriefed after their participation only if the study places them at high risk

questions.explanation:
Debrie�ng of research participants is addressed in Standard 8.08 of the APA's Ethics Code and Principles II.44 and III.26 of the Canadian Code
of Ethics. Standard 8.08 of the Ethics Code requires psychologists to inform participants promptly following their participation in the study
about its nature, results, and conclusions; and Principle III.26 of the Canadian Code of Ethics requires psychologists to debrief participants as
soon as possible after their involvement in a study when there has been incomplete disclosure about the study's purpose. Consequently, of the
answers given, this one is most consistent with ethical guidelines.
Answer B: Weighing perceived harm is not included in the language of the ethics codes regarding debrie�ng participants.
Answer C: Debrie�ng is always required when deception is used in research studies.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect, as the guidelines require participants to be debriefed as soon as possible when they have participated in a
study where deception was used.

questions.question: A psychologist should be aware that information contained in client records _________________________________.

options.A: is protected by law and can never be disclosed without the client's consent
options.B: is the property of the psychologist and cannot be disclosed without his/her consent
options.C: is the joint property of the psychologist and client and cannot be disclosed without the consent of both
options.D: is not free from disclosure all of the time, regardless of the wishes of the client or the psychologist

questions.explanation:
Con�dentiality of client information is waived in certain situations in the military and privilege is waived in certain legally de�ned situations.
Therefore, this is the best answer choice.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. There are some situations when client information must be released, despite the wishes of the client or the
psychologist. Record ownership and access are governed by legal guidelines.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. In most jurisdictions, the laws grant ownership of the physical record to the practitioner but give clients the
right to have access to the information contained in the record.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. There are times when other individuals or entities have the right to access client information.

questions.question: A psychologist in private practice is going through a di�cult divorce and, as a result, has started drinking and is often depressed. He should do which of the following?

options.A: plunge deeper into his work to take his mind off his own problems
options.B: seek professional consultation and consider temporarily suspending his practice
options.C: explain the situation to his clients and offer to refer them to other therapists
options.D: immediately refer his clients to other therapists

questions.explanation:
This issue is addressed by Standard 2.06(b) of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle II.11 of the Canadian Code of Ethics. According to the APA
Ethics Code, the psychologist should take appropriate action, which may include, "obtaining professional consultation or assistance ... to
determine whether they should limit, suspend, or terminate their work-related duties" [Ethics Code, Standard 2.06(b)]. Psychologists do not
necessarily have to abandon their professional practice when experiencing a period of personal distress. However, when personal problems
may be adversely affecting the welfare of their clients, psychologists must take appropriate action.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. Seeking consultation with another professional is the best answer.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. This may be necessary at some point, but the best initial step would be to seek consultation to determine
the most appropriate course of action.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. Seeking professional consultation would be the appropriate �rst step.

questions.question: A psychology intern offers his supervisor a chance to invest in a real estate business. The supervisor _____________________________.

options.A: should consult a colleague regarding this decision
options.B: should invest but only in his wife's name
options.C: should refuse to invest
options.D: should report the intern to the ethics committee

questions.explanation:
Multiple relationships are addressed in Standard 3.05 of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle III.33 of the Canadian Code of Ethics. Standard
3.05 states that "a psychologist refrains from entering into multiple relationships if the multiple relationships could reasonably be expected to
impair the psychologist's objectivity, competence, or effectiveness in performing his or her functions as a psychologist, or otherwise risks
exploitation or harm to the person with whom the professional relationship exists." Principle III.33 of the Canadian Code of Ethics includes a
similar requirement. The situation described in this question represents a multiple (dual) relationship that could potentially impact the
psychologist's ability to remain objective when acting as a supervisor for the intern.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. Ethics codes clearly direct psychologists to avoid multiple relationships that will compromise their
objectivity.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. Any �nancial entanglement with a supervisee signi�cantly risks compromise in the psychologist's
competence and objectivity.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. It would be a better strategy for the supervisor to educate the intern about multiple relationships rather than
report the intern to the ethics committee.

questions.question: Dr. Molly Mendez, a well-known behavioral psychologist, is asked by her secretary if she would be willing to provide him with therapy to overcome gambling addiction. If Dr. Mendez agrees to do so, she will be acting ____________________________.

options.A: ethically as long as she has expertise in treating gambling addiction
options.B: ethically as long as she charges the secretary her usual fee for psychological services
options.C: unethically since doing so is likely to create an unacceptable multiple relationship
options.D: unethically since maintaining the secretary's con�dentiality will be di�cult in this situation

questions.explanation:
The situation described in this question represents a multiple relationship. Multiple relationships are addressed in Standard 3.05 of the APA's
Ethics Code and Principle III.33 of the Canadian Code of Ethics. These guidelines prohibit multiple relationships that could be expected to
impair a psychologist's objectivity, which is a potential problem in this situation since the roles of employer and therapist would continue
simultaneously over an extended period of time.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect as Dr. Mendez would be acting as both employer and therapist if she agrees to see her secretary in therapy.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect because it does not address the potentially harmful multiple relationship described in this question.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect because this answer fails to take into account the primary ethical dilemma presented.

questions.question: Dr. Dennis Jones, in having a casual talk with a colleague, takes an idea from their conversation and decides to design and conduct a study to follow-up on the idea. When publishing the results of the study, it would be best for Dr. Jones to ___________________________.

options.A: offer his colleague joint authorship as �rst author
options.B: offer his colleague joint authorship as second author
options.C: acknowledge his colleague's contribution in a footnote or introductory statement
options.D: publish the study without acknowledging his colleague since the colleagues contribution was minor

questions.explanation:
This issue is addressed by Standard 8.12 of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle III.7 of the Canadian Code of Ethics. Standard 8.12(b) states
that publication credit must "accurately re�ect the relative scienti�c or professional contributions of the individuals involved, regardless of their
relative status"; and Principle III.7 states that psychologists "give credit for work done or ideas contributed by others ... in proportion to their
contribution."
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. While the idea for the study came from the colleague, she did not participate in designing or carrying out
the study and it would be acceptable to acknowledge her contribution in an introductory statement or footnote. This answer is incorrect.
Answer B: This answer incorrect. If the colleague does not contribute to the study by means of conducting or writing up the study, a footnote is
su�cient.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. The ethical guidelines clearly address giving publication credit relative to another's contributions.

questions.question: A psychologist is writing a book for distribution and illustrates the section on projective personality tests with a number of pictures used in the Hand Test. This use of test materials in this way is _______________________.

options.A: clearly unethical because it compromises the usefulness of the test
options.B: ethical only if the publisher of the book has accepted responsibility for including the pictures
options.C: ethical since the Hand Test is not a commonly used psychological test
options.D: professionally questionable but not covered by ethical guidelines

questions.explanation:
This answer is most consistent with the provisions of Standard 9.11 of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle IV.11 of the Canadian Code of
Ethics. Standard 9.11 states that "psychologists make reasonable efforts to maintain the integrity and security of test materials and other
assessment techniques"; and Principle IV.11 states that psychologists "protect the skills, knowledge, and interpretations of psychology from
being misused, used incompetently, or made useless (e.g., loss of security of assessment techniques) by others."
Answer B: This answer is incorrect as it fails to take into account test security.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. Whether a test is used frequently or not is irrelevant to the ethical question in this question.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect, given the ethical guidelines prioritize the integrity and security of test materials.

questions.question: Dr. Beatrice Bowen, a licensed psychologist, has been contacted by a company to evaluate job applicants. The job will involve administering projective tests to applicants for an accountant position to determine their sexual orientation. Dr. Bowen should ____________________.

options.A: not accept the job because the evaluation she is being requested to conduct represents an invasion of privacy
options.B: not accept the job because projective tests have been shown to be unreliable and invalid
options.C: accept the job and administer the tests as required but explain their purpose to all applicants before doing so
options.D: accept the job, administer the tests as required, and report the results to the company

questions.explanation:
Sexual orientation is not relevant to the ability to perform an accountant job successfully, and to seek such information as part of a job-related
assessment is clearly an invasion of privacy. Standard 9.04(b) of the APA's Ethics Code, for example, states that "psychologists may refrain
from releasing test data to protect a client/patient or others from substantial harm or misuse or misrepresentation of the data or the test"; and
Principle I.38 of the Canadian Code of Ethics states that psychologists "take care not to infringe ... on the personal, developmentally, or
culturally de�ned private space of individuals or groups unless clear permission is granted to do so."
Answer B: This answer is incorrect, as it fails to address the primary ethical con�ict presented.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect, given it does not acknowledge the unethical nature of the request.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect and not consistent with ethical guidelines.

questions.question: A client is in therapy with you as part of the requirements for her probation. During the third therapy session, she tells you that she wants to quit therapy. You should _________________________.

options.A: tell her that she cannot do so
options.B: tell her that she can quit but that she needs to consider the legal rami�cations of doing so
options.C: tell her that her desire to quit is normal resistance and that she should come to therapy for at least two more sessions before making a decision
options.D: call her probation o�cer immediately

questions.explanation:
The situation described in this question is addressed by Standard 3.07 of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle I.26 of the Canadian Code of
Ethics. This answer is most consistent with Standard 3.07 and Principle I.26, which address a psychologist's responsibilities when providing
services at the request of a third party. In this situation, the psychologist must ensure that the client understands what legal sanctions she may
face if she does not stay in therapy.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. The client may quit therapy, but there will be legal consequences as a result.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect as it overlooks the critical ethical issue inherent in this situation.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect, as it is aligned with neither ethical nor legal mandates.

questions.question: A ___________ is a person appointed by the court to represent and make decisions in a legal proceeding for a minor or another person legally incapable of doing so.

options.A: testamentary guardian
options.B: guardian ad litem
options.C: conservator of a minor
options.D: special conservator

questions.explanation:
The description presented in this question best describes a guardian ad litem who is appointed by the court for a speci�c purpose, such as to
make decisions for someone who is incapable of doing so. Additional information about guardianship is provided in the Ethics Manual of the
written study materials.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. A testamentary guardian is a person who is appointed in a deed or will to serve as guardian of a minor or
disabled person.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect. A conservator of a minor is responsible for managing the minor's �nances.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. A special conservator carries out the terms of preliminary protective orders.

questions.question: Dr. Dolores Del Rio has been seeing Jeff J. in therapy for four months. For the last month, Jeff has complained about the progress he is making in therapy, and Dr. Del Rio has responded by working with him to modify treatment goals. In the last therapy session, however, Jeff stated that he is not happy with therapy. Dr. Del Rio's best course of action would be to ___________________.

options.A: recognize that Jeff's concerns are a normal reaction to the changes he is making as the result of therapy
options.B: make a clinical decision as to whether or not Jeff is actually bene�ting from therapy and, if he is, encourage him to continue with therapy for at least several more sessions
options.C: discuss Jeff's continued dissatisfaction with him and the possibility of terminating therapy
options.D: tell Jeff that she is ethically required to terminate therapy with him since he is not satis�ed with the progress he is making

questions.explanation:
This question addresses the issue of terminating therapy when a client does not seem to be bene�ting from it. This is the best answer of those
given because it takes the client's welfare into consideration and is most consistent with ethical guidelines regarding termination of
professional services [see Standard 10.10(a) of the APA's Ethics Code or Principle II.37 of the Canadian Code of Ethics].
Answer A: The client's dissatisfaction may be related to several different factors, but the critical ethical issue in this question deals with the
matter of terminating therapy.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect. Given the client's concerns expressed over a month and the fact that the therapist has already adjusted
treatment goals, it is best to discuss termination with the client.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect because it fails to take into account the need for further discussion between the client and therapist.

questions.question: Dr. Donald Jackson is starting a therapy group for recently divorced men. He tells the editor of the local newspaper, who has just divorced his wife, that he can attend the group for free if the editor includes an article about the program in the newspaper. Dr. Jackson has acted ____________________.

options.A: ethically since his request does not violate ethical guidelines
options.B: ethically as long as the editor accurately describes the program
options.C: unethically because his request is exploitative and violates ethical guidelines
options.D: unethically only if the arrangement negatively impacts his objectivity when working with the editor in therapy

questions.explanation:
Of the answers given, this one is most consistent with ethical guidelines. Standard 5.02(b) of the APA Ethics Code prohibits psychologists from
compensating "employees of press, radio, television, or other communication media in return for publicity in a news item." Principle III.31 of the
Canadian Code of Ethics prohibits psychologists from exploiting "any relationship established as a psychologist to further personal, political, or
business interests at the expense of the best interests of their clients.
Answer A: Incorrect, because offering therapy in exchange for free publicity violates ethical guidelines.
Answer B: This answer is incorrect because it fails to address the ethical con�ict inherent in offering therapy in exchange for coverage in the
newspaper.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect as the psychologist would not want to engage in any arrangement that might impact his objectivity.

questions.question: You are hired as a psychology adjunct professor to teach a course at a graduate school. Which of the following are you ethically required to do in this case?

options.A: provide accurate information about the course content and be sure it is available for all interested parties
options.B: con�rm that the course content addresses the most recent research and theory in the area
options.C: con�rm that the course content addresses the interests of the students who enroll in the class
options.D: allow students an opportunity to evaluate you at the end of the semester

questions.explanation:
This issue is addressed by Standard 7.02 of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle III.5 of the Canadian Code of Ethics. Ethical guidelines
explicitly require psychologists to provide interested parties (in this case, the school administration and the students) with accurate and
complete information about the course content.
Answer B: Incorrect, because although presenting the most recent research and theory is usually a good idea, the importance of doing so
would depend on the nature of the class. For example, recent research and theory would not be covered in a "history of psychology" class.
Answer C: This answer is incorrect because the interests of the students do not necessarily coincide with the content that you, as the
instructor, believe is important to present.
Answer D: This answer is incorrect. Providing students with opportunities to evaluate the course is desirable but is not required by ethical
guidelines.

questions.question: In general, which of the following is considered the "best defense" for a psychologist who is being sued for malpractice?

options.A: adequate records
options.B: a signed informed consent
options.C: providing state-of-the-art services
options.D: good malpractice insurance

questions.explanation:
Most experts agree that good record-keeping is the best defense for practitioners in cases of litigation. In addition to being familiar with
relevant laws and ethical guidelines, the best way to reduce vulnerability to malpractice is maintaining adequate records.
Answer B is incorrect. While documenting informed consent is required by ethical standards, the practice alone does not provide a better
defense than accurate and detailed case records.
Answer C is incorrect. Adequate records are the best defense in the event of litigation.
Answer D is incorrect because while good malpractice insurance is usually wise, it will only help protect the clinician from fees incurred and will
not impact the outcome of litigation.

questions.question: A 26-year-old client you have been seeing for two months unexpectedly admits to you that he had sexual relations with the 15-year old daughter of his neighbor six months ago. He says that he knows what he did was wrong and that he will never do it again. You should __________________________________.

options.A: maintain the client's con�dentiality
options.B: report the client to the appropriate authorities
options.C: alert the parents of his victim
options.D: report the client to the appropriate authorities and alert the parents of his victim

questions.explanation:
In cases of known and suspected child abuse, a psychologist is legally and ethically required to make a report to the appropriate authorities.
Answer A: This answer is incorrect. As mandated reporters, psychologists are required by law to report child abuse.
Answer C: This does not account for the psychologist's duty to report known or suspected child abuse to the appropriate authorities.
Answer D: This may result in breaching the client's con�dentiality.

questions.question: A consulting �rm hired Dr. Sam Stone to assist with an ongoing research project. Dr. Stone works under the project director, Dr. Thompson, an organizational psychologist. Dr. Thompson asks Dr. Stone to review the preliminary report she has prepared for the project; and, in doing so, Dr. Stone discovers that some of the reported data is misleading and inaccurate. Dr. Stone expresses his concerns to Dr. Thompson and is told that "it will be taken care of." Subsequently, Dr. Stone learns that the report was submitted to the company without any changes. Dr. Stone reviews the ethical guidelines and decides that pursuing the matter further isn't necessary. Dr. Stone's conclusion is _________________________.

options.A: correct since this situation is not covered by ethical guidelines
options.B: correct since he has already attempted to resolve the matter in an informal manner as proscribed by ethical guidelines
options.C: correct since it is the project directors responsibility to provide the company with complete and accurate data
options.D: incorrect because he has a responsibility to ensure that the company is provided with complete and accurate data

questions.explanation:
This issue is addressed by Standard 1.01 of the APA's Ethics Code and Principle II.5 of the Canadian Code of Ethics. Answer D is most
consistent with the "spirit" of these guidelines. Speci�cally, Standard 1.01 of the Ethics Code states that "if psychologists learn of misuse or
misinterpretation of their work, they take reasonable steps to correct or minimize the misuse or misrepresentation." Principle II.5 of the
